summary: Redwood demo of hosted embeddings + reranking for Omnify's search relevance use case. Focus: two-stage retrieval (vector store + reranker), cost/latency tradeoffs, hosted API trial, next steps for benchmark POC and security docs.
topics: Latency vs cost tradeoffs and batching/quantization
transcript: [00:00] Liam Torres: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Liam from Redwood, this is Priya on the SE side. Can you all hear us OK?
[00:12] Sarah Chen: Yep, sounds good. Sarah here. We're excited — we've got search relevance issues with our product search. Hoping to see embeddings + rerank flow.

[00:28] Liam Torres: Great. Quick agenda: a short intro, demo of the hosted embeddings endpoint, then the rerank endpoint and how you'd wire it into a two-stage retrieval flow, and then Q&A and next steps.
[00:45] Priya Nair: I'll jump into the demo. First question — what's the current stack? Sarah?

[00:51] Sarah Chen: We're using Elastic for inverted index + a small ANN overlay (we tried a managed vector store, Pinecone for a POC), but latency at scale is a concern and quality varies. Dev handles ML infra details.

[01:10] Dev Patel: Yeah we have a batch pipeline to produce embeddings via OpenAI today, store vectors in Elastic + HNSW, then a light learned reranker. Costs are creeping up and we see mismatch on tail queries.

[01:30] Priya Nair: OK — that's exactly the use case Redwood hosted API is aimed at. For demo we'll show: embeddings generation (one endpoint), approximate retrieval in your vector store, then call Redwood's rerank endpoint to re-score top candidates. We also have an end-to-end hosted search path if you want fully managed vectors.
[01:52] Sarah Chen: Quick clarifying q: when you say rerank endpoint, is that a model that does cross-encoder scoring? Latency will be my main worry.

[01:59] Priya Nair: Yes — rerank is a cross-encoder style model. Typical pattern: retrieve top N (say 100) by ANN, then call rerank to score top K (10-20) with a cross-encoder. We provide batch rerank API so you can send multiple query-candidate pairs in one call to amortize overhead.
[02:18] Dev Patel: How does the hosted API handle batching? We have bursty traffic — would want to control latency SLOs.

[02:26] Liam Torres: We provide request-level config. For hosted, you can choose latency SLO targets; we do continuous batching behind the scenes and you can set a max wait threshold. If you need guaranteed throughput/latency, Dedicated reserved capacity is an option.
[02:48] Maya Ortiz: Any rough numbers you can share for embedding cost and rerank latency? Even ballpark for 768-d embeddings vs 1536.

[02:56] Priya Nair: Sure. Ballpark: 768-d embeddings ~ $0.0008 per 1k; 1536 maybe 1.5-2x that depending on model. Rerank cross-encoder latency ~30-120ms per pair on hosted depending on model size; with batch endpoints you can rerank 10-20 pairs in under 200ms typically. These are representative — we'll send exact pricing sheet.
[03:24] Sarah Chen: Sounds reasonable. What about vector dimension and metric — do you recommend cosine or dot?

[03:30] Priya Nair: We typically use cosine for normalized embeddings, dot for some model variants; key is consistency between embedder and ANN index. For your current pipeline, we can keep same dims — we also provide conversion helpers in the SDK.
[03:46] Dev Patel: There's often a mismatch between ANN ranking and cross-encoder. How do you recommend tuning top-N and rerank K?

[03:54] Priya Nair: Start with retrieve top 100 with HNSW, rerank top 10. In Optimize we can run offline evals on your relevance labels and recommend N/K per latency budget. Also caching common queries' rerank results reduces load.
[04:12] Liam Torres: I'll pause and show the console briefly — pull up the hosted API docs and a quick code snippet for embeddings call (he shares link: https://redwood.dev/embed-demo).

[04:25] [screen share noise / brief pause] Priya Nair: Here is the curl/SDK example: POST /v1/embeddings with input: [your text], model: 'rw-embed-768'. Response returns vector array. Then send vector to your ANN store.
[04:48] Sarah Chen: And the rerank flow?

[04:52] Priya Nair: Example: POST /v1/rerank with query and candidates payload. We accept candidate text, metadata, and can return scores + explanation tokens. We also support batch payloads so one request contains multiple query/candidate pairs.
[05:10] Dev Patel: You mentioned explanations — are those token-level attributions? That could help debugging relevance.
[05:18] Priya Nair: Yes we have optional explain flags. They add some latency, but useful during model tuning. We'll demo a quick rerank run with a sample query.
[05:30] [demo] Priya runs a live rerank on a sample product query; some slight audio lag. Output shows candidate list with scores and short explanation snippets.
[07:02] Sarah Chen: Output looks promising. A few questions on security: where do embeddings persist? We need SOC2, SSO, and KMS for encryption key control.

[07:14] Liam Torres: For hosted, by default ephemeral embeddings are not retained unless you choose to store vectors in Redwood-managed vector store. We are SOC2 Type II compliant; support SAML/SSO and allow KMS for Private deployment. We'll attach our security pack.
[07:34] Dev Patel: If we do a POC, we'd prefer not to push PII to managed vector store; can we run embeddings via hosted but store vectors in our own VPC-hosted store?

[07:43] Priya Nair: Absolutely — many customers use hosted API for embedding generation and store vectors in their own VPC or on-prem ANN. We also provide Private deployment if you want entirely customer-managed runtime.
[08:00] Maya Ortiz: Regarding metrics — we'll want per-query latency percentiles and token-level cost breakdowns for the POC. Does your console surface that?
[08:06] Liam Torres: Yes Console provides token-level cost estimates, per-route latency, and traces. Optimize will give batching/quantization suggestions tied to your latency budget.
[08:20] Dev Patel: One of our concerns is failing gracefully — if rerank is down or slow, do you provide fallbacks?

[08:28] Priya Nair: We have smart routing — if a cross-encoder is unavailable, you can fallback to a lighter rerank model or just return ANN scores. Also config for automatic fallback policies and A/B rollouts.
[08:45] Sarah Chen: Let's talk POC scope and success metrics. For us: increase MRR conversion on search by 6% and reduce median query time under 120ms for user-facing searches.

[08:59] Liam Torres: Good measurable goals. For scope we recommend: 10k documents, run baseline with your current pipeline, then run a Redwood-hosted embed + rerank trial to measure MAP@10 and latency budget. We'll help set up the benchmark script.
[09:18] Dev Patel: How close are the hosted API models to open checkpoints? Any chance of model drift or changes during POC?

[09:25] Priya Nair: We pin model versions per deployment. Hosted models are versioned and you can lock to a specific model hash. We also provide model release notes and ability to run canary rollouts.
[09:40] Sarah Chen: Any mention of cost controls? We need to cap spend during POC.
[09:46] Liam Torres: You can set rate limits and budget alerts in Console. We'll propose a limited trial with spend cap and monitor usage.
[09:55] Maya Ortiz: Can you walk through a sample POC timeline?

[10:00] Liam Torres: Week 0: sign NDA and get trial key, Week 1: ingest sample data + baseline run, Week 2: run Redwood embedding+rerank tests, Week 3: optimize and tune with Optimize recommendations, Week 4: results and decision. We can compress depending on resources.

[10:20] Priya Nair: A couple technical notes — for large docs we recommend chunking and using chunk-level embeddings with rerank at passage level. Also enable prefix KV caching for repeated queries to lower cost.
[10:38] Dev Patel: For the rerank batch API, what's the max payload size? We hit 10MB sometimes.
[10:44] Priya Nair: For hosted, default is 8MB payload; we can increase for Dedicated. We'll share exact limits in the doc.
[10:55] Sarah Chen: You mentioned Optimize earlier — what kind of model/quantization recs do you give?

[11:02] Priya Nair: Optimize analyzes your latency and accuracy curves and suggests quantization (e.g., 8-bit int), smaller model variants for rerank where quality tradeoff is acceptable, and batching configs. It ties recommendations to unit cost impact.
[11:20] [short silence / typing] Liam Torres: I'll show the demo deck link (slides) and a benchmark spreadsheet example (link: https://redwood.dev/benchmarks/omnify-sample).
[11:35] Maya Ortiz: Nice — can we see an example of a bad-case query where embedding-only fails and rerank helps?

[11:42] Priya Nair: Sure — here's a sample: query "red running shoes for plantar fasciitis" where ANN returns generic running shoes. Reranker surfaces specific rehab-focused shoes with higher precision. Demo shows improvement in MAP@5.
[12:10] Dev Patel: Any notes on GDPR / data residency? We have EU customers and need logs in EU region.
[12:16] Liam Torres: We have region controls for hosted. For strict residency customers we suggest Private deployment or Dedicated capacity pinned to region. We'll attach a short GDPR/residency FAQ.
[12:30] Sarah Chen: Great. A few nitty-gritty items: sample code for SDK, sample metrics dashboard, and the security pack — please send.
[12:38] Liam Torres: Yep will send: pricing, trial key, security docs, and Priya will send benchmark script.
[12:45] Maya Ortiz: If we sign for Dedicated later, what's the lead time?
[12:49] Priya Nair: Depends on capacity, typically 2-6 weeks; we'll flag that to the capacity team if you indicate interest.
[13:00] [brief pause] Liam Torres: Quick open Qs?
[13:05] Dev Patel: Are there any known integrational gotchas with our current Elastic+HNSW setup?
[13:12] Priya Nair: Watch for vector normalization mismatch and ensure the same distance metric. Also tune efSearch/efConstruction — but those are ANN-side. We'll provide a checklist.
[13:30] Sarah Chen: Ok let's confirm the POC metrics: MAP@10 improvement, conversion lift, and p50 latency under 120ms.
[13:38] Liam Torres: Noted. We'll include instrumented dashboards in the POC.
[13:45] Maya Ortiz: One last: who's the exec sponsor on Redwood side for the POC?
[13:49] Liam Torres: I'll be primary AE, Priya SE, and I'll loop in Solutions Eng and Customer Success once we sign.

[14:00] Priya Nair: I'll attach the benchmark harness — it's a python script that runs embeddings, stores vectors, and runs rerank comparisons. It logs MAP/NDCG/latency. We'll pre-fill with example configs.
[14:15] [background chatter] Dev Patel: Good — we'll aim to give you the 10k dataset by next Wednesday.
[14:23] Liam Torres: Great; next steps recap coming up. Any other concerns?
[14:30] Sarah Chen: Only legal — we need an MSA draft before starting.
[14:34] Liam Torres: Understood — I'll have legal share a template and redaction notes.

[14:40] [closing] Liam Torres: Ok recapping next steps: 1) Liam send pricing + trial key + security pack; 2) Priya share benchmark script and console walkthrough materials; 3) Omnify to provide sample dataset and success metrics. Follow-up demo scheduled Aug 19. Any disagreements?
[14:58] Maya Ortiz: All good from product. Thanks everyone.
[15:02] Dev Patel: Thanks, looking forward to the trial.
[15:07] Sarah Chen: Thanks — bye.
[15:10] [meeting end]
